PC Jeweller is debt free. But your shares fell twenty three percent from the high. Why? Part two.
Quick recap. In 2018, it sold nine thousand crore of jewellery. By 2024, sales crashed to six hundred crore, with a big loss.
Then the comeback. Profit of five seventy eight crore in FY25, seven fourteen crore in FY26, and three thirty one crore this quarter alone.
Borrowings fell from four thousand one fifty crore in 2024. All fourteen banks were repaid, ahead of schedule. Debt free, says the company.
Next, up to a hundred new showrooms in eighteen months, a new brand for young buyers, and one forty two crore collected from old export dues.
The stock went from seven rupees to twenty this year. Now it's near fifteen. So what's the catch?
Dilution. To clear the banks, the company issued new shares. Share capital more than doubled since 2024. Promoters now own just thirty nine percent.
And sales are still a third of 2018. Eleven lakh people own it now, up from two lakh. The turnaround is real. A multibagger is not proven.
